summary.title: Adventures in Rust: A Basic 2D Game
summary.one_liner: Learn how a beginner built a simple Defender-inspired 2D shooter in Rust using the Piston game framework, covering rendering, input, traits, collision detection and text.
keywords: how to make a game in rust
takeaways: Piston can be used as a modular Rust game framework that abstracts windowing and input, with a render/update event loop.
Rust traits such as a GameObject trait let different on-screen objects share render, update and collision behavior.
Circle-based collision detection checks whether bullets and enemies overlap using their positions and radii.
Text and score rendering in Piston needed a font loaded through GlyphCache, and the author found the docs outdated.
Rust felt familiar to C-style programmers, and Cargo was praised as a useful build and dependency tool; Rust game dev was noted as still maturing.
summary.summary: The author, coming from Python and JavaScript, walks through building a very basic 2D shooter inspired by Defender while learning Rust. The post uses the Piston framework, splitting logic into lib.rs and main.rs, and shows code for the render and update loops, keyboard input, a GameObject trait, circle collision checks, score text with a bitmap font, and win/lose states. It ends with an appendix of learnings about Rust's syntax, the Cargo tool, and the immaturity of Rust game libraries at the time.
